tool_schemas.name: get_service_status
tool_schemas.description: Current version per region, health and error rate of a service.

tool_schemas.name: list_deployments
tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18). v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy in production. Per runbook, I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent production release that was healthy, in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Post-rollback status: healthy=true, error rate 0.002, all regions on v2.3.0. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 failure before any redeploy. Note that v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging.

args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18). v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy in production. Per runbook, I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent production release that was healthy, in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Why v2.3.0:** It is the most recent production release marked healthy. v2.3.1 is unhealthy in production, so I did not use it.
- **Result:** checkout-api now reports healthy on v2.3.0 with an error rate of 0.002, down from 0.18 on v2.3.1.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback, and the post-rollback status. The first attempt to open it timed out. I retried with the same idempotency key, and the retry returned a single incident.

Follow-up: v2.3.1 needs investigation before anyone redeploys it. Its release candidate v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging.

content.text: The most recent production release that was healthy is v2.3.0 (v2.3.1 is unhealthy in production). I'll roll back to it.
